fields.Frequency: ~10–15 new leases/year (aligned with 10–15 new stores/year growth target)
fields.Participants: COO, Legal Counsel, CFO, VP Store Operations, Landlord
fields.Trigger: New store or DC location approved by real estate team (W1652 site selection)
fields.Volume: Each lease negotiation covers 1 property; lease term typically 5–15 years

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-assign of "assignment and subleasing rights" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews lease agreement" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-create of "creates lease liability and ROU asset per PFRS 16 in BuildRight Property…" (replaces manual Step 5).
Controls: - CTL-367 (ensure controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1).)
- operational: COO / Legal Counsel review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Landlord leverage in high-demand locations**: Prime commercial lots in Metro Manila and Cebu command premium rents and landlords may resist exclusivity clauses, escalation caps, or early termination provisions

- **PFRS 16 balance sheet impact**: Long-term leases create significant lease liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet; each new store lease adds PHP 20–50M in lease liabilities, affecting debt-to-equity ratios and banking covenants

- **Title verification risk**: Incomplete or fraudulent property titles in provincial areas can lead to legal disputes after lease execution and store construction investment; thorough title verification through the Registry of Deeds is essential; mitigated by CTL-367 (controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1))
Staffing Implication: - **COO**: Lease negotiation is a core responsibility; ~10–15 negotiations/year × 4–8 weeks each = near-full-time during peak expansion periods
- **Legal Counsel**: Lease review adds ~1–2 weeks per negotiation; absorbed within Legal team (may require external real estate counsel for complex negotiations at ~PHP 100K–300K per lease)
- No incremental headcount beyond existing roles
System Touchpoints: - Lease management module: lease register with key dates, terms, financial obligations (W1854.5c)
- PFRS 16 lease accounting: ROU asset and lease liability creation (W1854.5d)
- Property master data: location, landlord, property specifications (W1854.5c)
- Approval workflow for lease commitments (W1854.4e)
- Integration with W1652 (site selection), W20 (construction), W275 (IFRS 16 lease accounting), W40 (capex — tenant improvements)
Time Estimate: - Total per lease: ~8–15 weeks elapsed; ~40–80 hours active time

steps.activity: COO identifies and shortlists candidate properties per W1652 (site selection): (a) location criteria: population density, trade area demographics, accessibility (highway frontage, public transport), proximity to competitors, (b) property specifications: selling area 8,000–15,000 sqm, adequate parking (100–200 slots), loading dock access for delivery trucks, zoning compliance (commercial), (c) ownership verification: clean title, no encumbrances, tax declarations current

COO conducts preliminary lease negotiation with landlord: (a) rental rate per sqm (benchmark: PHP 300–800/sqm/month depending on location; Metro Manila premium), (b) lease term and renewal options (target: 10–15 years with 5-year renewal options), (c) annual escalation rate (typical: 3–5% per annum or CPI-linked), (d) tenant improvement allowance (landlord contribution to store fit-out), (e) common area maintenance (CAM) charges, (f) exclusivity clause (no competing hardware/home improvement tenant in same development), (g) early termination provisions, (h) assignment and subleasing rights

Legal Counsel drafts/reviews lease agreement: (a) Philippine legal compliance: Civil Code provisions on lease contracts, (b) IFRS 16 / PFRS 16 implications: classification as operating lease vs. finance lease, right-of-use (ROU) asset and lease liability accounting, (c) force majeure clause: typhoon, earthquake, pandemic provisions, (d) dispute resolution: arbitration vs. litigation, jurisdiction, (e) building permits and occupancy permits: landlord responsibility for securing, (f) insurance requirements: fire, earthquake, liability coverage minimums, (g) data privacy: landlord access to tenant premises and customer data considerations

CFO reviews financial terms: (a) total lease obligation: monthly rent × 12 months × lease term + escalation, (b) NPV of lease payments for PFRS 16 lease liability calculation, (c) impact on BuildRight Property Management, Inc. cash flow and intercompany settlement with BuildRight Depot, Inc., (d) comparison to benchmark rents in same area, (e) approval: lease commitments > PHP 50M require CEO approval; > PHP 200M require Board approval

Lease execution: (a) COO and Legal Counsel coordinate lease signing with landlord, (b) notarization per Philippine legal requirements, (c) lease agreement registered in lease management module in ERP, (d) Finance creates lease liability and ROU asset per PFRS 16 in BuildRight Property Management, Inc. books, (e) COO coordinates tenant fit-out with landlord and store construction team per W20 (real estate & construction)

fields.Frequency: ~10–15 new leases/year; ongoing management of ~205 active leases
fields.Participants: Lease Administrator, Legal Counsel, COO, Finance

workflows.name: Lease Agreement Registration, Document Management & Key Date Tracking

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scanned signed lease agreement, notarized copy" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "generates automated alerts for key lease dates" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "Lease Administrator conducts annual lease file audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Missed renewal deadlines**: If the lease administrator misses a renewal option deadline, the lease may auto-expire or the landlord may demand significantly higher rent for renewal; automated alerting with 12-month advance notice is critical
- **Document loss**: Physical lease agreements may be lost in provincial offices; digitized document management with backup is essential for a 200-store chain
Staffing Implication: - **Lease Administrator**: Dedicated role managing ~205 active leases; annual registration, alert management, and audit add ~10–15 hours/month. Can be a dedicated position within Finance or Real Estate team, or absorbed by Finance Manager with ~20% allocation.
System Touchpoints: - Lease register with full key date calendar and automated alerting (W1855.1–2)
- Document management for lease agreements and amendments (W1855.1e)
- Rent schedule management with escalation tracking (W1855.2b)
- Integration with W275 (PFRS 16 lease accounting), W317 (bank account/signatory management — security deposits)

steps.activity: Lease Administrator registers new lease in lease management module: (a) lease number, landlord, property address, entity (BuildRight Property Management, Inc.), (b) key dates: commencement, expiry, renewal option deadline, rent escalation dates, break clause dates, (c) financial terms: base rent, CAM charges, escalation schedule, security deposit, (d) special conditions: exclusivity, TI allowance, maintenance responsibilities, (e) document attachment: scanned signed lease agreement, notarized copy

System generates automated alerts for key lease dates: (a) renewal option deadline: 12 months before lease expiry (option exercise deadline typically 6–9 months before expiry), (b) rent escalation: 90 days before escalation effective date, (c) lease expiry: 18 months before expiry for renewal or relocation planning, (d) break clause window: 6 months before break option deadline, (e) insurance renewal: 60 days before property insurance expiry, (f) landlord permit/license expiry: 60 days before expiry

Lease Administrator conducts annual lease file audit: (a) verify all key dates are current and accurate, (b) verify all amendments and modifications are recorded, (c) verify rent schedule matches current lease terms (including all escalations applied), (d) verify landlord contact information is current, (e) verify insurance certificates on file and current, (f) flag any leases with upcoming critical dates for action

fields.Frequency: ~15–25 lease renewals/year (based on ~205 active leases with 10–15 year terms; some shorter)
fields.Participants: COO, Legal Counsel, CFO, Store Operations, Landlord
fields.Trigger: System alert: renewal option deadline approaching (12 months before lease expiry)
fields.Volume: 1 property per renewal; renewal typically 5–10 years

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-issue of "COO evaluates renewal options 12 months before" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-request of "request landlord contribution to store renovation/refresh for renewal…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews and executes renewal agreement" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-367 (ensure controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1).)
- operational: COO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Renewal rent shock**: Landlords in high-growth areas (e.g., Bonifacio Global City, Cebu IT Park) may demand 30–50% rent increases at renewal; without competitive alternatives, BuildRight faces margin erosion
- **Relocation cost**: Moving a store costs PHP 10–30M (new fit-out, inventory relocation, temporary closure, customer communication); renewing at a higher rent may be cheaper than relocating
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by COO, Legal, and Finance
System Touchpoints: - Lease renewal alert and tracking (W1856.1 trigger)
- Store performance analytics for renewal decision (W1856.1a)
- PFRS 16 lease liability recalculation for renewed terms (W1856.3b)
- Integration with W67 (store performance), W702 (new store opening), W703 (store closure), W275 (IFRS 16 accounting)
Time Estimate: - Total per renewal: ~6–10 weeks elapsed; ~30–50 hours active time

steps.activity: COO evaluates renewal options 12 months before lease expiry: (a) store performance: sales per sqm, profitability, foot traffic trends — is this store worth renewing? (b) market rent benchmarking: has the area appreciated? What are current market rents for comparable properties? (c) landlord relationship: any recurring issues (maintenance, disputes, access problems)? (d) alternative locations: are there better properties available in the same trade area? (e) decision: (i) renew at current location, (ii) renegotiate terms, (iii) relocate to alternative, (iv) close store (if underperforming per W703)

If renewing: COO negotiates renewal terms with landlord: (a) target: maintain or reduce current rent; leverage store improvement to area (increased foot traffic, commercial activity) as negotiation tool, (b) renewal rent escalation: negotiate cap on escalation increase for renewal term, (c) TI refresh: request landlord contribution to store renovation/refresh for renewal commitment, (d) extended term: negotiate longer renewal term (10+ years) for rent stability

Legal Counsel reviews and executes renewal agreement; Finance updates lease terms in system: (a) update lease end date and financial schedule, (b) recalculate PFRS 16 ROU asset and lease liability for renewed term, (c) update key date alerts in lease management module

If relocating: COO initiates W1854 (new site lease negotiation) for alternative location and coordinates W1857 (lease termination) for current location; Store Operations coordinates store transition per W703 (store closure) and W702 (new store opening)

fields.Participants: COO, Legal Counsel, Store Operations, Finance, VP Store Operations
fields.Trigger: Store closure decision (W703); lease expiry without renewal; early termination per lease clause

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews termination provisions in lease agreement" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-issue of "issues formal termination notice to landlord per lease provisions" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document condition, agree on restoration scope" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-367 (ensure controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1).)
- operational: COO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Restoration cost**: Returning a warehouse-format retail space to "original condition" can cost PHP 2–5M (removing installed shelving, electrical, paint, signage); negotiate restoration scope early during lease signing (W1854) to limit obligations
- **Security deposit disputes**: Landlords may claim damages exceeding fair wear and tear to withhold security deposits; photographic condition documentation at move-in and move-out is essential
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by existing COO, Legal, Store Operations, and Finance roles
System Touchpoints: - Lease termination workflow with notice tracking (W1857.2)
- PFRS 16 lease derecognition processing (W1857.4a)
- Asset recovery and redistribution integration with W45, W703
- Security deposit tracking and return processing (W1857.3e)
- Integration with W703 (store closure), W45 (inventory redistribution), W275 (PFRS 16 accounting), W39 (asset disposal)
Time Estimate: - Total: ~8–14 weeks elapsed; ~40–60 hours active time

steps.activity: COO reviews termination provisions in lease agreement: (a) notice period required (typically 6–12 months for early termination; 3–6 months for non-renewal at expiry), (b) early termination penalty (if applicable): typically 3–6 months' rent or unamortized TI allowance, (c) restoration obligations: condition in which property must be returned to landlord (original condition minus fair wear and tear), (d) security deposit return conditions
COO issues formal termination notice to landlord per lease provisions; Legal Counsel reviews notice for compliance with lease terms and Civil Code requirements

Store Operations coordinates move-out: (a) store closure per W703 (store closure, consolidation & asset recovery), (b) inventory redistribution to other stores or DC per W45 (closure redistribution), (c) fixture and equipment removal: reusable fixtures relocated; permanent modifications restored per landlord requirements, (d) property handover walkthrough with landlord representative: document condition, agree on restoration scope, (e) coordinate security deposit return

Finance processes termination accounting: (a) derecognize PFRS 16 ROU asset and lease liability, (b) recognize termination gain/loss, (c) process early termination penalty payment if applicable, (d) process security deposit return, (e) update lease register: close lease record

Post-termination: (a) Legal Counsel confirms all obligations fulfilled; landlord provides written release, (b) COO archives terminated lease file, (c) if relocation: coordinate with W702 (new store opening) for replacement location

fields.Participants: Lease Administrator, COO, Store Managers, Legal Counsel
fields.Trigger: Ongoing relationship management; maintenance requests; dispute resolution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "maintains landlord communication log" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-submit of "submits maintenance request to landlord with SLA" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Quarterly landlord performance review" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-367 (ensure controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1).)
- operational: Lease Administrator review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Slow landlord response**: Provincial landlords may be unresponsive to maintenance requests; buildings deteriorate, affecting customer experience and safety; SLA tracking and escalation are essential

- **Maintenance responsibility ambiguity**: Lease agreements may have unclear boundaries between landlord and tenant maintenance responsibilities (e.g., HVAC, signage electrical); clear responsibility matrix should be established at lease signing
Staffing Implication: - **Lease Administrator**: Landlord communication management is a core function; ~50–100 interactions/month × 15–30 min each = ~12.5–50 hours/month — absorbed by dedicated Lease Administrator role
System Touchpoints: - Landlord communication log integrated with lease management module (W1858.1)
- Maintenance request tracking with SLA timers (W1858.2)
- Landlord scorecard module (W1858.3)
- Dispute register with escalation workflow (W1858.4)
- Integration with W47 (facility maintenance), W116/W117 (real estate & construction per VS-20)

steps.activity: Lease Administrator maintains landlord communication log: (a) all correspondence logged in system: date, subject, communication type (email, phone, in-person), participants, (b) open issues tracked with status: pending landlord action, pending BuildRight action, resolved, (c) landlord contact information kept current

Maintenance issue resolution: (a) Store Manager reports maintenance issue to Lease Administrator: (i) structural issues (roof leaks, wall cracks, floor damage) — landlord responsibility per most lease agreements, (ii) building systems (electrical supply, water, sewage, fire suppression) — landlord or shared responsibility, (iii) parking lot and exterior maintenance — landlord responsibility, (b) Lease Administrator submits maintenance request to landlord with SLA: urgent (safety/operational impact) — 48 hours; standard — 7 days; (c) if landlord unresponsive: escalate to COO for formal demand letter; Legal Counsel involved if health/safety risk

Quarterly landlord performance review: (a) Lease Administrator compiles landlord scorecard: (i) maintenance responsiveness, (ii) building condition, (iii) CAM service quality (cleaning, security, parking), (iv) communication responsiveness, (v) compliance with lease terms, (b) COO reviews underperforming landlords: formal communication requesting improvement; consideration at lease renewal (W1856)

Dispute resolution: (a) if informal resolution fails: Legal Counsel issues formal demand letter, (b) if landlord disputes maintenance responsibility: Legal Counsel reviews lease agreement and advises, (c) if dispute escalates: mediation per dispute resolution clause in lease; arbitration if mediation fails, (d) COO maintains dispute register with status and resolution timeline

fields.Trigger: Business need to modify lease terms (space reduction/expansion, rent restructuring, use change)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-collect of "COO identifies modification need" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document all agreed changes in lease amendment" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-schedule of "schedule and lease term" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-367 (ensure controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Landlord resistance to modification**: Landlords may refuse space reduction or rent restructuring, especially in high-demand locations; modification negotiation leverage depends on market conditions and remaining lease term

- **PFRS 16 remeasurement complexity**: Lease modifications trigger remeasurement of the ROU asset and lease liability under PFRS 16; complex modifications (partial termination + expansion) require careful accounting treatment
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by COO, Legal, and Finance
System Touchpoints: - Lease amendment management with version control (W1859.3)
- PFRS 16 lease modification accounting (W1859.4b)
- Rent schedule update in AP module (W1859.4d)
- Integration with W275 (PFRS 16 accounting), W7C (recurring rent payments)
Time Estimate: - Total: ~6–10 weeks elapsed; ~20–40 hours active time

steps.activity: COO identifies modification need: (a) space reduction: store underperforming and excess space can be surrendered, (b) space expansion: adjacent space available for store expansion, (c) rent restructuring: temporary rent relief during economic downturn or pandemic, (d) use change: add warehouse space or click-and-collect area, (e) subleasing: surplus space to be subleased to complementary tenant

COO negotiates modification terms with landlord: (a) space reduction: pro-rata rent reduction; target minimum 15–20% rent reduction for 20–30% space surrender, (b) space expansion: rent increase per current sqm rate; negotiate TI allowance for expansion area, (c) rent restructuring: temporary reduction with step-up schedule back to normal, (d) document all agreed changes in lease amendment

Legal Counsel drafts lease amendment: (a) specify modification effective date, (b) updated rent schedule and lease term (if changed), (c) updated space measurements (if space changed), (d) any new conditions or waived provisions, (e) both parties execute amendment; notarized per Philippine legal requirements

Finance updates lease records: (a) update lease schedule in system with modified terms, (b) recalculate PFRS 16 ROU asset and lease liability, (c) post any modification gain/loss, (d) update rent payment schedule

fields.Trigger: Surplus space available for sublease; assignment to another BuildRight entity
fields.Volume: Typically surplus backroom or office space at store locations

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "verify sublease is permitted under master lease" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-submit of "submit sublease request to landlord with proposed subtenant and terms" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "record sublease income" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-367 (ensure controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1).)
- operational: COO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Master lease risk**: Subtenant actions that violate the master lease (e.g., unauthorized alterations, noise complaints, safety violations) can jeopardize BuildRight's own lease; careful subtenant selection and monitoring is essential; mitigated by CTL-367 (controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1))

- **Subtenant default**: If subtenant stops paying rent, BuildRight must still pay full rent to landlord while pursuing subtenant through legal channels; sublease security deposit mitigates but does not eliminate this risk
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by existing COO, Legal, and Finance roles
System Touchpoints: - Sublease register linked to master lease (W1860.4)
- Sublease income tracking and AP/AR management (W1860.5)
- PFRS 16 sublease accounting module (W1860.4b)
- Integration with W275 (PFRS 16 accounting), W235 (transfer pricing), W14 (IC transactions)
Time Estimate: - Sublease identification and landlord approval: 3–6 weeks
- Ongoing management: ~2–4 hours/month per active sublease
- Total per sublease: ~6–10 weeks elapsed for setup; ~30–50 hours/year ongoing

steps.activity: COO identifies surplus space: (a) store backroom larger than needed for inventory operations, (b) office space above minimum requirement, (c) adjacent space acquired with lease but not needed for retail operations, (d) verify sublease is permitted under master lease (most leases require landlord consent)

COO obtains landlord consent for sublease: (a) submit sublease request to landlord with proposed subtenant and terms, (b) negotiate landlord's consent fee (if any — typically 1 month's sublease rent or PHP 50K–100K), (c) confirm landlord retains right to approve/reject subtenant

Legal Counsel drafts sublease agreement: (a) sublease area, term, rent, and conditions, (b) subtenant compliance with master lease terms (no violations that could jeopardize master lease), (c) maintenance responsibilities for subleased area, (d) sublease termination tied to master lease termination, (e) subtenant insurance requirements

Finance processes sublease accounting: (a) record sublease income, (b) PFRS 16 treatment: sublease classification (operating vs. finance) based on sublease terms relative to master lease, (c) intercompany sublease (if subtenant is another BuildRight entity): transfer pricing at arm's length per W235

Ongoing sublease management: (a) Lease Administrator collects sublease rent monthly, (b) monitors subtenant compliance with sublease terms, (c) if subtenant defaults: Legal Counsel initiates sublease termination and eviction per Philippine law

fields.Trigger: Monthly reporting cycle; quarterly board review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generates lease portfolio dashboard" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-forecast of "forecast" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "undiscounted" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-367 (ensure controlled execution — Lease Negotiation & Administration (PA-42.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data accuracy**: Lease portfolio dashboard is only as good as the underlying lease data; inaccurate rent schedules or missing escalation records produce misleading analytics
Staffing Implication: - **FP&A**: Lease portfolio reporting adds ~1 day/month + 1 day/quarter + 1 week/year = ~25 days/year — absorbed by existing FP&A team
System Touchpoints: - Lease portfolio analytics dashboard (W1861.1)
- Rent-to-revenue ratio tracking by store (W1861.1b)
- Lease expiry calendar with renewal pipeline (W1861.1d)
- Landlord concentration analysis (W1861.2d)
- Integration with W35 (financial reporting), W275 (PFRS 16), W67 (store performance)

steps.activity: Monthly: FP&A generates lease portfolio dashboard: (a) total annual rent obligation by entity and landlord, (b) rent as % of revenue by store (target: rent ≤ 8–12% of store revenue for big-box retail), (c) PFRS 16 lease liability total and trend, (d) lease expiry profile: leases expiring in next 12, 24, 36 months with renewal status, (e) rent escalation schedule: upcoming escalations by month and amount, (f) stores where rent exceeds 12% of revenue (flag for renegotiation or relocation evaluation), (g) geographic concentration: rent exposure by region and landlord

Quarterly: FP&A and COO present portfolio analysis to CFO and COO: (a) rent vs. revenue trend by store cluster, (b) upcoming lease expirations and renewal strategy, (c) market rent comparison: are BuildRight leases at, above, or below market?, (d) landlord concentration risk: what % of total rent is owed to top 5 landlords?, (e) capital expenditure forecast: upcoming TI refresh needs, (f) recommendations: renegotiation targets, relocation candidates, closure candidates

Annually: FP&A prepares lease portfolio section for Board of Directors: (a) total lease commitment (undiscounted), (b) PFRS 16 lease liability impact on balance sheet, (c) 5-year lease expenditure forecast, (d) new store expansion impact on lease commitments, (e) portfolio optimization opportunities
